info.title: Infrastructure
info.description:
The CloudShare v4 REST API manages environments, their VMs and resources, and environment policies. It is served through the CloudShare API gateway:

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| Production | `https://api.accelerate.cloudshare.com` |
| Pre-production | `https://api.accelerate.preprod-use1.cloudshare.com` |

All paths start with `/v4/` (for example `GET /v4/environments`). Request and response bodies are JSON (`application/json`). Send `Accept: application/json`.

### Identifiers

Every entity id is an opaque external string. You never see a numeric database id. The first two characters of an id give the entity type:

| Prefix | Entity |
|---|---|
| `EN` | Environment |
| `PR` | Project |
| `BP` | Blueprint |
| `SS` | Snapshot |
| `PO` | Policy |
| `RE` | Region |
| `MC` | Virtual machine |
| `TM` | Team |
| `EC` | Public cloud (external cloud) |
| `CS` | Public-cloud creation script |

If an id is malformed, or its prefix is the wrong type for the parameter (for example a `PR...` id where an environment id is expected), the request fails with `400 Bad Request`. The error is keyed to the parameter name, for example `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}`. Users are identified by email address, not by id.

### Authentication

Get an access token with the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant. Use your API ID as `client_id` and your API key as `client_secret`: `POST {baseUrl}/v4/oauth/token` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and body `grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<API ID>&client_secret=<API key>`. The response contains `access_token`, `token_type` (`Bearer`) and `expires_in` (seconds). Send the token on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. The token is an encrypted JWT, so treat it as opaque. Request a new token when it expires.

### Errors

Most validation and business-rule errors return a JSON object that maps a field name to a list of messages. For example: `{"name": ["'name' must not be empty."]}`. The empty key `""` holds errors that are not tied to one request field. Authentication failures and unexpected server errors use a `{"message": "...", "code": "0x..."}` object. Some `403` and `404` responses have an empty body.

parameters.name: OwnerEmail
parameters.description: Only environments whose owner's email contains this value (substring match).

parameters.name: SponsoredLoginToken
parameters.description: Only the environment that has this sponsored login token (exact match).

parameters.name: MachineVanity
parameters.description: Machine vanity host name; only the part before the first `.` is matched. When it matches a machine, only that machine's environment is returned; when it matches no machine, this filter is ignored.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: When `true`, `count` holds the total number of matching environments before paging. Defaults to `false`, in which case `count` is `null`.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Number of environments to skip. Must be 0 or greater. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: Limit
parameters.description: Page size. Must be 1 or greater. Defaults to 100; values above 100 are reduced to 100.

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: `field`, `field:asc` or `field:desc` (single field). Fields: `name`, `status`, `ownerEmail`, `startTime`, `expirationTime`. Defaults to `name:asc`. Do not send a comma-separated list: it is not rejected, but the resulting order is undefined.

400.description: `sortBy` is malformed (bad field characters, extra `:`, direction other than `asc`/`desc`) or names a field that is not allowed. Body: `{"": [message, ...]}`.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

get.description:
Returns a page of the environments visible to the caller, wrapped in `{count, items}`. No specific permission is needed; the result is limited to environments the caller can see. Only live environments are listed: deleted environments (expiration time in the past) and environments whose project has expired never appear.

Filters combine with AND. `ownerEmail` is a substring match on the owner's email, not an exact match. `sponsoredLoginToken` is an exact match. `machineVanity` takes a machine vanity host name and uses only the part before the first `.`; a name that matches no machine is ignored (no filtering).

Sorting uses `sortBy=field` or `sortBy=field:asc|desc`. Allowed fields (case-insensitive): `name`, `status`, `ownerEmail`, `startTime`, `expirationTime`. Default is `name:asc`. `sortBy` accepts a single field; do not send a comma-separated list: it is not rejected, but the resulting order is undefined. `status` uses a fixed status order (not alphabetical by the returned value). Any other field in the first token returns 400.

requestBody.description: Environment to create. `name` and `projectId` are required.

201.description: Environment created. The `Location` header contains the URL of the new environment.

400.description: Validation failed, keyed by field (e.g. `{"name": ["'name' must not be empty."]}`): missing body, `name` or `projectId`; an id with the wrong type prefix (`projectId` PR, `regionId` RE, `policyId` PO, `teamId` TM, `blueprintId` BP, `snapshotId` SS, `externalCloudId` EC, `scriptId` CS); a null label or a label containing a comma; duplicate `externalCloudId`; `policyId` not in the project. Or a business rule failed (body `{"": [message]}`): duplicate environment name, region not available to the project, quota exceeded, creator/owner not project members or sharing no team, team not in project, invalid `scriptId`, invalid Terraform variables.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: No create permission in the project (empty body); a credit card is required for the subscription; the creator's role does not allow creating for `ownerEmail`; or the blueprint is disabled for environment creation.

404.description: `ownerEmail` user not found; owner is not a member of `teamId`; blueprint not found; snapshot not available in the selected region.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

post.description:
Creates an environment in a project, either empty (no `blueprintId`) or from a blueprint, optionally from a specific `snapshotId` of it. Returns 201 with the new environment and a `Location` header pointing to it. Provisioning continues after the response; poll `GET /v4/environments/{id}` for its `status`.

The body is validated first (400), because the permission target `projectId` is in the body. The caller then needs the project's *Create environment from blueprint* permission (default: Team Member and above) when `blueprintId` is given, or *Create environment from scratch* (default: Project Manager and above) when it is not; otherwise 403 with an empty body. An unknown `projectId` also yields 403.

Defaults: `regionId` defaults to the default VMware region; `policyId` defaults to the project's default policy. A `policyId` that is not in the given project (or not visible to the caller) is rejected with 400 on `policyId`. `snapshotId` is ignored unless `blueprintId` is also set. The name must be unique (case-insensitive) among the owner's current environments.

`ownerEmail` creates the environment for another user: an unknown email returns 404; both users must be members of the project; without `teamId` they must share a team; the creator must be at least Team Manager (in that team, unless Project Manager) and their role must be at least the owner's (403 otherwise).

put.description:
Replaces the environment's `name`, `description` and `labels` and returns the updated environment. Omitted or null `description`/`labels` are cleared. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient.

The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs. The body is validated afterwards: `name` is required and non-empty; labels must not contain commas. Blank labels are dropped and the rest trimmed. The name must be unique (case-insensitive) among the owner's current environments. If the environment's details cannot be edited in its current state, 400 is returned.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or `changes` missing, unsupported `op`, unsupported `path` (`{"": [message, ...]}`); or validation failed (empty name, label with a comma); or duplicate name / details not editable in the current state.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: The caller lacks edit permission on the environment. Empty body.

404.description: No environment with this id exists (empty body), or it is not visible to the caller as a project environment (`{"": ["Environment not found"]}`).

patch.description:
Partially updates an environment and returns it. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

Body: `{"changes": [{"op": 2, "path": "/name", "value": "New name"}]}`. Only the `replace` operation (`2`) is supported; any other operation returns 400. Writable paths: `/name`, `/description`, `/labels` (array of strings). Do not send other paths: depending on the path they are ignored or rejected with 400. A missing `changes` array returns 400; an empty array changes nothing. After applying, the same validation as PUT runs (non-empty name, no commas in labels), then the name-uniqueness and editability rules.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or the environment's state does not allow deletion (`{"": [message]}`).

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: Caller lacks edit permission (empty body) or delete permission on the environment.

404.description: No environment with this id exists. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

500.description: Showcase environment, environment shared with a project, or non-deletable environment the caller cannot configure (`{"": [message]}`); a delete already in progress; or an unexpected failure.

delete.description:
Starts deleting the environment and returns 204. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. In addition the project's *Delete environment* permission (default: Team Member and above) must allow it, otherwise 403. The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

The environment's state must allow deletion (400 otherwise); a delete already in progress returns 400. Showcase environments, environments shared with a project and non-deletable environments cannot be deleted. If the owner is an end user and this is their last active environment in the project, the owner's project membership is removed as well.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Required. ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Window start. Environments whose expiration time is on or after this moment are included.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Required. ISO 8601 date-time, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Window end. Environments whose start time is on or before this moment are included. Must not be earlier than `from`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of environments to skip. Defaults to 0; negative returns 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1â€“1000. Defaults to 1000; 0, negative or above 1000 returns 400.

parameters.name: subscriptionId
parameters.description: Subscription id (`SB...`) whose usage records are read. Optional when the caller is Project Manager in exactly one subscription.

400.description: `from` later than `to`; negative `offset`; `limit` not in 1â€“1000; malformed `subscriptionId`; or `subscriptionId` omitted while the caller manages more than one subscription. Body `{"": [message, ...]}`.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: Caller is not a Project Manager in any subscription, or not in the given `subscriptionId`.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

get.description:
Returns lifetime resource-usage totals for the environments visible to the caller whose lifetime overlaps the `from`â€“`to` window, ordered by creation time. The window only selects environments; the metrics are totals over each environment's whole life, not over the window. This endpoint returns no total: `count` is `null`.

The caller must be a Project Manager in a subscription: `subscriptionId` must be one of those subscriptions (403 otherwise). When `subscriptionId` is omitted, the caller's single such subscription is used; none returns 403 and more than one returns 400. Metrics come only from the selected subscription; the environment list itself is not restricted to it, so listed environments with no usage recorded there have `null` metrics.

Unlike other list endpoints, `limit` is validated rather than capped: it must be 1â€“1000 (default 1000).

get.description:
Returns a page of the environment's VMs, wrapped in `{count, items}`. Requires view permission on the environment (the caller must be able to see it). The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

`sortBy` accepts one or more comma-separated `field[:asc|desc]` tokens, applied in order. Sortable fields (case-insensitive): `id`, `name`, `description`, `status`, `suspensionState`, `memoryState`, `progress`, `imageId`, `os`, `webAccessUrl`, `fqdn`, `externalAddress`, `username`, `password`, `consoleToken`. `internalAddresses`, `resources` or an unknown field return 400. Without `sortBy` the order is unspecified.

Items include connection credentials (`username`, `password`, `consoleToken`); `password` and `consoleToken` are only filled once the VM is ready.

get.description: Returns one VM of the environment. Requires view permission on the environment (the caller must be able to see it). The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs. `vmId` is then checked: it must be a machine (`MC`) id (400 otherwise) and must belong to this environment (404 otherwise).

204.description: Resume started, or the environment was already running.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or the status is not `suspended`/`ready`/`preparing` (`Action is not available in the current Environment state`), or quota exceeded.

post.description:
Resumes a suspended environment and returns 204. The operation is asynchronous; poll `GET /v4/environments/{id}` for the status. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

Calling it on an environment that is already `ready` or `preparing` does nothing and still returns 204. Any other status returns 400. Exceeding the subscription's resource quota returns 400.

parameters.name: immediate
parameters.description: Reserved for CloudShare staff; other callers should omit it. Defaults to `false`.

204.description: Suspend started, or the environment was already suspended.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or the environment's state does not allow suspending.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: Caller lacks edit permission (empty body) or is not allowed to suspend this environment.

404.description: No environment with this id exists. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

post.description:
Suspends a running environment and returns 204. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. The caller must also be allowed to suspend this environment (403 otherwise). The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

An environment that is already `suspended` is left as is (204). If the current state does not allow suspending, 400 is returned. `immediate` is reserved for CloudShare staff; other callers should omit it.

200.description: Postponed. `message` holds the minutes remaining until the inactivity action, as a string.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or the environment is not `ready` or has no scheduled inactivity action.

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: The caller cannot view the environment. Empty body.

404.description: No environment with this id exists. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

post.description:
Pushes the environment's scheduled inactivity action to a platform-configured number of minutes from now (never past the end of the current run, and never earlier than already scheduled) and returns the minutes now remaining. Repeated calls do not add up. Requires view permission on the environment (the caller must be able to see it). Edit permission is not required. The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

Only available when the environment is `ready` and an inactivity action is scheduled; otherwise 400.

requestBody.description: Optional. `snapshotId` selects the snapshot; omit the body or the field to use the blueprint's default snapshot.

204.description: Revert started (or one was already in progress).

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or the backend rejected the revert because of the environment's state (`{"": [message]}`).

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: Caller lacks edit permission (empty body) or is not allowed to revert this environment.

404.description: Environment not found (empty body), or `snapshotId` is not a usable snapshot of the environment's blueprint.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

500.description: The environment's status does not allow reverting, the environment has no snapshots, or the revert failed unexpectedly. Body: `{"": [message]}`.

post.summary: Revert an environment to a snapshot
post.description:
Reverts the environment's machines to a snapshot of its blueprint and returns 204. The revert runs asynchronously. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. The caller must also be allowed to revert this environment (403 otherwise). The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

The body is optional. Without `snapshotId` the blueprint's default snapshot is used. A given `snapshotId` must be a ready snapshot of the environment's blueprint that the caller may use; otherwise 404. A revert already in progress is not an error (204). If the environment has no snapshots or its status does not allow reverting, 500 is returned.

requestBody.description: Optional custom extension amounts. Omit to extend by the policy defaults.

400.description: `id` is empty, malformed or not an environment (`EN`) id. Body: `{"id": ["Id has incorrect format"]}` (or `"Environment ID hasn't been provided"`). Or a time span is missing/malformed, exceeds the policy, runtime exceeds storage, or the state does not allow extending (`{"": [message, ...]}`).

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

403.description: Caller lacks edit permission (empty body) or extend-with-policy permission; extension blocked by deprovisioning.

404.description: No environment with this id exists. Empty body.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

post.description:
Extends the environment's runtime (current run) and storage (expiration) and returns 204. Requires edit permission on the environment: the project's role-based *Edit environment* setting for the environment's team (default: Project Manager and above) combined with the caller's role in the environment. Under the default setting, owning the environment is not sufficient. The caller must also be allowed to extend with the environment's policy (403 otherwise). The id format (400), existence (404) and permission (403) are checked before the action runs.

The body is optional. With no extensions the environment is extended by the policy's full runtime and storage durations. To extend by custom amounts, send **both** `runTimeExtension` and `storageTimeExtension` as time spans (`[d.]hh:mm[:ss]`, e.g. `02:00:00`, `1.00:00:00`); sending only one returns 400. Each value may not exceed the policy's runtime/storage duration, and the runtime extension may not exceed the storage extension (400 otherwise). The environment's state must allow extending (400); an extension blocked by account deprovisioning returns 403.

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: When `true`, the response's `count` holds the total number of matching policies before paging. Defaults to `false`, and then `count` is `null`.

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort order, written as `field` or `field:asc` / `field:desc`. The direction is not case-sensitive and defaults to ascending. You can give several keys separated by commas, e.g. `name:desc,id`. Allowed fields: `name` and `id`. An unknown field or a malformed value returns 400. Defaults to `name`.

parameters.name: Search
parameters.description: Free-text search. Matches policies whose name contains this text; `%` and `_` act as wildcards.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Number of matching policies to skip. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: Limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of policies to return. There is no default and no cap: if you leave it out, every matching policy is returned.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Filter on policy name. A plain value matches the name exactly. Operators: `in(a,b)`, `notin(a,b)`, `contains(text)`; operator names are lowercase and spaces around values are ignored. In `contains`, `%` and `_` act as wildcards. To put a literal comma inside a value, write `%comma%`. Other operators (`between`, `gt`, `lt`) are not supported; they currently answer 500.

200.description: One page of policy summaries. `count` is `null` unless `count=true`.

400.description: `sortBy` is malformed or names a field that cannot be sorted (body `{"": [message]}`), or a filter value has the wrong format (keyed to the filter, e.g. `{"name": [message]}`).

401.description: The `Authorization` header is missing or malformed.

429.description: Too many failed requests from your IP address. Wait before retrying.

get.description:
Returns the active policies from every project where the caller is a Team Member or above. Deleted policies are left out. Each item is a brief summary; call **Get a policy** for durations, suspend and auto-action settings, and usage.

No extra permission is needed. A project where the caller has no role adds no items.

Results are sorted by `name` ascending unless you pass `sortBy`. If you pass it, only your order applies. Use `offset` and `limit` to page. There is no page-size cap, and leaving out `limit` returns every matching policy. The `name` and `search` filters are combined with AND. Query parameter names are not case-sensitive (`sortBy` and `SortBy` both work).

parameters.name: Count
parameters.description: When `true`, the response's `count` holds the total number of matching policies before paging. Defaults to `false`, and then `count` is `null`.

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: Sort order, written as `field` or `field:asc` / `field:desc`. The direction is not case-sensitive and defaults to ascending. You can give several keys separated by commas, e.g. `name:desc,id`. Allowed fields: `name` and `id`. An unknown field or a malformed value returns 400. Defaults to `name`.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Number of matching policies to skip. Defaults to 0.

parameters.name: Limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of policies to return. There is no default and no cap: if you leave it out, every matching policy is returned.

put.description:
Replaces every editable field of a policy. This is a full update: send all fields, under the same rules as **Create a policy**. Returns `200` with the resulting policy.

**Copy-on-write.** Changing `name`, `runtimeMinutes`, `storageMinutes`, `allowSuspend` or `suspendMinutes` does not edit the policy in place. The old policy is deleted and a new one is created with a new id. Classes and pending invitations that used the old policy move to the new one, and the response carries the new `id`, which differs from `{policyId}`. Environments created with the old policy stay on it, and the new policy's `usage` starts at 0. Changing only `autoAction` or `inactivityThresholdMinutes` normally updates the policy in place and also applies to environments currently using it. For running environments the new threshold is counted from the start of the current run (from now when switching from `alwaysOn`), so a shorter threshold can take effect immediately. Always use the `id` in the response, because any update can return a new id.

**In-use restriction.** While any current or scheduled environment uses the policy, you cannot change `runtimeMinutes`, `storageMinutes` or `allowSuspend`, nor `suspendMinutes` while suspend stays enabled. Such a request returns 400, with the error keyed to each changed field. You can still change `name`, `autoAction` and `inactivityThresholdMinutes`. Sending back unchanged values does not trip this restriction. `inactivityThresholdMinutes` is required whenever `autoAction` is not `alwaysOn`, even if **Get a policy** returned it as `null`.

Requires Project Manager in the policy's project. Checks run in this order: `policyId` format (400), whether the policy exists and is visible (404), permission (403), `projectId` format and body validation (400), whether the policy belongs to `projectId` (404), then name uniqueness and the in-use restriction (400). parameters.description: When true, `count` holds the total number of matching scripts; otherwise `count` is `null`.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Number of rows to skip. Defaults to 0; must not be negative.

parameters.name: Limit
parameters.description: Page size. Defaults to 50; must be positive and at most 100 (larger values are rejected).

parameters.name: SortBy
parameters.description: `field` or `field:desc`. Sortable fields are `name`, `createdAt` and `validationStatus`. Defaults to `createdAt:desc`.

parameters.name: ValidationStatus
parameters.description: Equality only; `valid` is the only accepted value.
